title: Board of Ethics complaints and confidentiality
summary: In November 2024 an attorney testified he was confused about where the Board of Ethics stood on a complaint, and the board approved a press release explaining why it keeps investigations confidential. In closed session the board denied one complaint, declined an opinion on another, combined two items and set one matter for an informal hearing still to come.

timeline.text: Closed-session item 4A(ii): The chair reported the board voted to decline review of another matter for lack of jurisdiction and refer it to another investigating body.
Closed-session item 4A(i): The chair reported the board voted to set one closed-session matter for an informal hearing.
Motion confirming the executive session decisions: In open session, the board voted to confirm the decisions reported from the closed session.
Item 5B3: In closed session, the board voted to set item 5B3 for an informal hearing.
Item 5B2: In closed session, the board voted to deny the complaint in item 5B2.
Item 5B1: In closed session, the board voted to decline to give an opinion on item 5B1.
Consolidation of two complaint items: In closed session, the board voted to combine two agenda items into one matter.
Item 5A1, request for reconsideration: In closed session, the board voted to deny reconsideration on item 5A1.
Motion to approve and distribute a press release on confidentiality of board investigations: The board approved a press release explaining its confidentiality rules and asked that it be sent out.
Staff will add two changes to the press release about finding past minutes and meeting recordings.
A member moved to approve a press release explaining why the board keeps its investigations confidential.
During public testimony, an attorney said he was confused about where the board stood in reviewing a complaint.
